stem: A new mobile app's shopping cart stores each cart as a single item retrieved by a unique cart ID, at a scale that could grow from a handful of users to millions overnight, with no ability to forecast that growth in advance.

choices.text: Amazon RDS for MySQL with a fixed instance class sized for current traffic
Amazon Redshift for the cart data
Amazon DynamoDB in provisioned capacity mode with a fixed throughput setting
Amazon DynamoDB in on-demand capacity mode

rationale: A cart retrieved by a single unique key at unpredictable, potentially explosive scale is the key-value access pattern DynamoDB is built for, and on-demand capacity mode scales instantly with no capacity planning, matching the inability to forecast growth. A fixed relational instance class has to be sized in advance and cannot absorb an overnight jump from a handful of users to millions. Redshift is built for analytical queries over large datasets, not single-item lookups by key. DynamoDB provisioned capacity with a fixed throughput setting is the right service but the wrong mode for traffic that cannot be forecast.
